title: QuaNAS: Uncertainty-Aware Reuse of Earlier Searches for Query-Efficient Neural Architecture Search
abstract: arXiv:2610.31251v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Neural architecture search (NAS) on a new dataset often affords only tens of short training runs, so what the search knows before its first evaluation decides its efficiency. Yet most NAS methods start from scratch, guided at best by zero-cost proxies that are unreliable across tasks. QuaNAS treats a library of earlier searches in the same search space as explicit knowledge of uncertain reliability. Main effects of design decisions learned from this library and, secondarily, zero-cost proxies become priors over candidate architectures without any label of the new dataset. A Gaussian process starts at the prior optimum and re-estimates after every evaluation how far each prior is trusted. Under a protocol frozen before any confirmation data were seen, QuaNAS was evaluated once on 12 new image, time-series, text and tabular datasets. It lowered anytime regret on the short-training objective 2.7- to 3.9-fold relative to five pre-specified N

translated_title: QuaNAS：面向查询高效神经架构搜索的、具有不确定性感知的早期搜索复用
translated_abstract: 在全新数据集上进行神经架构搜索（NAS）时，往往只有几十次短时训练的机会，因此搜索在首次评估之前所掌握的知识决定了其效率。然而，大多数NAS方法都是从零开始，充其量只依靠零成本代理指标来引导，而这些指标在不同任务间的可靠性参差不齐。QuaNAS将同一搜索空间中以往的搜索库视为可靠性不确定的显式知识。从该搜索库中学习到的设计决策的主效应，以及（次要的）零成本代理指标，在完全不使用新数据集任何标签的情况下，构成候选架构上的先验分布。高斯过程从先验最优解出发，并在每次评估后重新估计对各先验的信任程度。在一个在任何确认数据出现之前就已冻结的评估协议下，QuaNAS在12个全新的图像、时间序列、文本和表格数据集上各评估了一次。相比五个预先指定的NAS基线，它将短时训练目标下的任意时刻遗憾降低了2.7至3.9倍。
tldr: QuaNAS将以往搜索的“设计决策主效应”和零成本代理指标转化为候选架构的不确定性先验，并利用高斯过程在每次评估后动态校准对各先验的信任程度，从而在完全不使用新数据集标签的情况下，将查询高效神经架构搜索的任意时刻遗憾降低2.7至3.9倍。
en_tdlr: QuaNAS converts knowledge from earlier searches—the main effects of design decisions and zero-cost proxies—into uncertainty-aware priors over candidate architectures, and uses a Gaussian process to re-calibrate trust in these priors after every evaluation, lowering anytime regret by 2.7–3.9x for query-efficient NAS on 12 new datasets without using any labels from them.
